input.quote: In the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.1 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
input.rationale: Section 14.2.1 requires PB (our party) to pay SFJ 300% of all Development Costs paid or incurred, accelerated and due within days of SFJ terminating for our material breach, and Section 14.4.2 confirms that this sum stands "in lieu of any claim for damages" — i.e. a liquidated amount payable by the customer on breach. A 3x multiple of the funder's outlay, triggered by breach and payable regardless of whether Regulatory Approval is ever obtained, is a penalty far beyond the playbook fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at a short fee equivalent) and can exceed the value remaining to us under the Agreement, which is walk-away territory. Given the existing bargain (SFJ funds the Clinical Trials and earns its return through contingent Approval Payments), the preferred position of no customer-payable liquidated amount is disproportionate, so we take the fallback and reduce the breach payment to a return of Development Costs actually paid or incurred — the same measure the parties already agreed in Section 14.2.9 — leaving SFJ's Approval Payment and Buy-Out economics intact. We have not re-flagged the parallel 300% amount in Section 14.2.2 (at-will termination), which is handled under the termination-for-convenience rule; the 25% interest uplift in Section 14.2.10 and the 150% multiples in Sections 14.2.6/14.2.8.1 are noted as related penalty mechanics we would expect to align on the same basis.

proposal.summary: Reduce the 300% multiple of Development Costs payable by PB on SFJ's termination for PB breach to a return of Development Costs actually paid or incurred.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a 300% multiple of Development Costs falling due on us within days of a termination for our breach; because Section 14.4.2 makes it SFJ's sole damages remedy, it operates as a penalty rather than compensation. We have reduced it to a return of the Development Costs actually paid or incurred (the same measure the parties already accepted in Section 14.2.9), leaving SFJ's contingent Approval Payments and Buy-Out economics untouched.

ops.oldText: an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination
ops.newText: an amount equal to one hundred percent (100%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination
